title: Principles of Information Security
subtitle: Guess the hidden phrases — spin for consonants, buy vowels, solve the puzzle

puzzles.hint: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability -- the three pillars of information security.
Layering multiple overlapping security controls so the failure of any one layer does not breach the system.
Tracks the state of active connections and only allows packets belonging to established sessions.
Manipulating people -- not systems -- to reveal credentials or grant access. Pretexting and phishing are prime examples.
The framework of CAs, certificates, and key pairs that enables trusted asymmetric encryption across the internet.
The structured process for containing, eradicating, and recovering from a ransomware encryption event.
Grant users only the minimum permissions required to perform their job -- reduces blast radius of a compromise.
Sophisticated, long-term campaigns -- often nation-state sponsored -- that emphasize stealth and persistence for months or years.
